# CircleCI testsuite

## `circleci testsuite <command> [flags]`

Reduce test execution time while maintaining test confidence by running CircleCI's testsuite tooling.

Available for free:
- Static test splitting - split tests evenly across parallel execution nodes using previous run timings.
- Manual rerun of failed tests - Rerun workflow from the CircleCI UI, API or CLI reruns only the tests that failed.

Available as opt-in paid features:
- Test impact analysis - run only the tests impacted by your code changes.
- Dynamic test splitting - distribute tests across parallel execution nodes as they run, reducing node idle time.
- Auto rerun failed tests - automatically rerun failed tests during your test run.

Each feature is independently enabled, configure them per suite in .circleci/test-suites.yml.

| Flag | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| `--local` | Use locally stored impact data for selection and analysis instead of fetching from CircleCI |
| `--verbose` | Enable verbose debug logging |

### `circleci testsuite list-tests <suite-name> [flags]`

List selected test atoms on stdout

| Flag | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| `--analyze-tests=all|impacted|none|default` | Which tests to analyze for generating impact data |
| `--run-tests=all|impacted|none|default` | Which tests to select and run |
| `-t, --test-atom-pattern=REGEXP` | Only consider discovered test atoms matching this regular expression |
| `--runner=auto|codeception|cucumber|cypress|django|exunit|gotestsum|gradle|jest|minitest|mocha|phpunit|playwright|pytest|rspec|vitest` | Test runner to use when the suite is not defined in .circleci/test-suites.yml. 'auto' detects the runner from the project files |

**Arguments:**

`<suite-name>` is the name of the test suite to run, matching a suite defined in .circleci/test-suites.yml.

### `circleci testsuite run <suite-name> [flags]`

Run a testsuite defined in .circleci/test-suites.yml

| Flag | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| `--analyze-tests=all|impacted|none|default` | Which tests to analyze for generating impact data |
| `--run-tests=all|impacted|none|default` | Which tests to select and run |
| `-t, --test-atom-pattern=REGEXP` | Only consider discovered test atoms matching this regular expression |
| `--runner=auto|codeception|cucumber|cypress|django|exunit|gotestsum|gradle|jest|minitest|mocha|phpunit|playwright|pytest|rspec|vitest` | Test runner to use when the suite is not defined in .circleci/test-suites.yml. 'auto' detects the runner from the project files |

**Arguments:**

`<suite-name>` is the name of the test suite to run, matching a suite defined in .circleci/test-suites.yml.

### `circleci testsuite doctor <suite-name> [flags]`

Run diagnostics to check your test suite setup

| Flag | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| `--json` | Output doctor results as JSON. Requires --doctor |
| `--runner=auto|codeception|cucumber|cypress|django|exunit|gotestsum|gradle|jest|minitest|mocha|phpunit|playwright|pytest|rspec|vitest` | Test runner to use when the suite is not defined in .circleci/test-suites.yml. 'auto' detects the runner from the project files |

**Arguments:**

`<suite-name>` is the name of the test suite to run, matching a suite defined in .circleci/test-suites.yml.

### `circleci testsuite impact [flags]`

(experimental) Explore test impact data: which files impact a test, and which tests a file impacts

| Flag | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| `--test=ATOM` | Print the files impacting this test atom |
| `--file=PATH` | Print the test atoms impacted by this file |
| `--key=KEY` | Impact data key to read |
| `--sort=name|impact` | Order by name, or by impact: most connected first |
| `--version=N` | Fetch a specific version of impact data instead of the latest |

### `circleci testsuite result <job-id> [flags]`

(experimental) Show how a job's test atoms were selected and how they ran

| Flag | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| `--test=ATOM` | Print the test results for this test atom |
| `--sort=name|time` | Order by name or time |

**Arguments:**

`<job-id>` Browse the test results for this job

### `circleci testsuite generate <suite-name> [flags]`

(experimental) Generate a .circleci/test-suites.yml file

| Flag | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| `--template=auto|codeception|cucumber|cypress|django|exunit|gotestsum|gradle|jest|minitest|mocha|phpunit|playwright|pytest|rspec|vitest` | specifies the test runner. |
| `--dry-run` | prints the suite instead of appending it to .circleci/test-suites.yml. |

**Arguments:**

`<suite-name>` is the name of the test suite to run, matching a suite defined in .circleci/test-suites.yml.

## Example Test Suites

Starter `.circleci/test-suites.yml` configurations for common test runners.

### Go with gotestsum

```yaml
---
name: ci tests
discover: go list -f '{{ if or (len .TestGoFiles) (len .XTestGoFiles) }} {{ .ImportPath }} {{end}}' ./...
run: go run gotest.tools/gotestsum@latest --junitfile="<< outputs.junit >>" -- -race -count=1 << test.atoms >>
options:
  store-test-results: true
```

### vitest

```yaml
---
name: ci tests
discover: npx vitest list --filesOnly
run: npx vitest run --reporter=junit --outputFile="<< outputs.junit >>" --bail 0 << test.atoms >>
options:
  store-test-results: true
```

### Jest

```yaml
---
name: ci tests
discover: npx jest --listTests
run: JEST_JUNIT_ADD_FILE_ATTRIBUTE=true JEST_JUNIT_OUTPUT_FILE="<< outputs.junit >>" npx jest --runInBand --reporters=jest-junit -- << test.atoms >>
options:
  store-test-results: true
```

### Mocha

```yaml
---
name: ci tests
discover: find ./test -type f \( -name '*.js' -o -name '*.cjs' -o -name '*.mjs' \) \( ! -path './test/*/*' -o -name '*.spec.*' -o -name '*.test.*' \)
run: npx mocha --reporter xunit --reporter-options output="<< outputs.junit >>",showRelativePaths << test.atoms >>
options:
  store-test-results: true
```

### Cypress

Add [cypress-circleci-reporter](https://www.npmjs.com/package/cypress-circleci-reporter) and `mocha` as dev dependencies. It writes a JUnit report per spec with each test's file, so point it at a directory output. The `[hash]` placeholder gives each spec its own file.

```yaml
---
name: ci tests
discover: find ./cypress/e2e -type f -name '*.cy.*'
run: |
  npx cypress run --reporter cypress-circleci-reporter \
      --reporter-options "resultsDir=<< outputs.junit-directory >>,resultFileName=result-[hash]" \
      --spec "$(echo << test.atoms >> | tr ' ' ',')"
options:
  store-test-results: true
```

### pytest

```yaml
---
name: ci tests
discover: find . -type f -name 'test*.py' \( -path './tests/*' -o -path './testing/*' \)
run: pytest --disable-pytest-warnings --no-header --quiet --tb=short --override-ini=junit_family=legacy --junit-xml="<< outputs.junit >>" << test.atoms >>
options:
  store-test-results: true
```

### RSpec

```yaml
---
name: ci tests
discover: find spec -type f -name '*_spec.rb'
run: bundle exec rspec --format RspecJunitFormatter --out "<< outputs.junit >>" << test.atoms >>
options:
  store-test-results: true
```

### PHPUnit

```yaml
---
name: ci tests
discover: find tests -type f -name '*Test.php'
run: vendor/bin/phpunit --log-junit "<< outputs.junit >>" << test.atoms >>
options:
  store-test-results: true
```

### ExUnit

Add [junit_formatter](https://hex.pm/packages/junit_formatter) as a test dependency and configure it in `config/test.exs`.

```elixir
config :junit_formatter,
  report_dir: System.get_env("JUNIT_REPORT_DIR", "_build/test"),
  include_filename?: true
```

```yaml
---
name: ci tests
discover: find test -type f -name '*_test.exs'
run: JUNIT_REPORT_DIR="<< outputs.junit-directory >>" mix test --formatter JUnitFormatter --formatter ExUnit.CLIFormatter << test.atoms >>
options:
  store-test-results: true
```

### Cucumber

```yaml
---
name: ci tests
discover: find features -type f -name '*.feature'
run: bundle exec cucumber --format junit,fileattribute=true --out "<< outputs.junit-directory >>" << test.atoms >>
options:
  store-test-results: true
```

### Playwright

Playwright reports each test file relative to its `testDir`, so discover lists files from there. Change `tests` if your `testDir` is different.

```yaml
---
name: ci tests
discover: cd tests && find . -type f -name '*.spec.*' | sed 's|^\./||'
run: PLAYWRIGHT_JUNIT_OUTPUT_FILE="<< outputs.junit >>" npx playwright test --reporter=junit << test.atoms >>
options:
  store-test-results: true
```

### Gradle

Gradle has no command-line flag for its JUnit report directory, so expose one in your `build.gradle.kts`.

```kotlin
tasks.test {
    providers.gradleProperty("junitDir").orNull?.let {
        reports.junitXml.outputLocation.set(file(it))
    }
}
```

```yaml
---
name: ci tests
discover: find src/test -type f \( -name '*Test.java' -o -name '*Tests.java' -o -name '*Test.kt' -o -name '*Tests.kt' \) | sed -E -e 's#^src/test/(java|kotlin)/##' -e 's#\.(java|kt)$##' -e 's#/#.#g'
run: gradle test --rerun -PjunitDir="<< outputs.junit-directory >>" $(printf -- '--tests %s ' << test.atoms >>)
options:
  store-test-results: true
```

### Django

Add [unittest-xml-reporting](https://pypi.org/project/unittest-xml-reporting/) and configure it in your Django settings.

```python
TEST_RUNNER = "xmlrunner.extra.djangotestrunner.XMLTestRunner"
TEST_OUTPUT_DIR = os.environ.get("JUNIT_OUTPUT_DIR", "test-reports")
```

```yaml
---
name: ci tests
discover: find . -type f \( -name 'test_*.py' -o -name 'tests.py' -o -name 'tests_*.py' \) -not -path './.venv/*' | sed 's|^\./||'
run: JUNIT_OUTPUT_DIR="<< outputs.junit-directory >>" python manage.py test $(echo << test.atoms >> | tr ' ' '\n' | sed -e 's|\.py$||' -e 's|/|.|g')
options:
  store-test-results: true
```

### Minitest

Add [minitest-ci](https://github.com/circleci/minitest-ci) to your Gemfile, then enable it and set its report directory in `test/test_helper.rb`.

```ruby
require "minitest/ci"
Minitest.load :ci if Minitest.respond_to?(:load) # Minitest 6 no longer loads plugins automatically
Minitest::Ci.report!
Minitest::Ci.report_dir = ENV.fetch("JUNIT_REPORT_DIR", "test/reports")
```

```yaml
---
name: ci tests
discover: find test -type f \( -name '*_test.rb' -o -name 'test_*.rb' \) -not -name 'test_helper.rb'
run: JUNIT_REPORT_DIR="<< outputs.junit-directory >>" bundle exec ruby -Itest -e 'ARGV.each { |f| require File.expand_path(f) }' << test.atoms >>
options:
  store-test-results: true
```

### Codeception

Add a `circleci` group to your `codeception.yml` for the run command to fill with test atoms.

```yaml
groups:
  circleci: tests/_output/circleci
```

```yaml
---
name: ci tests
discover: find tests -type f -name '*Cest.php'
run: |
  printf '%s\n' << test.atoms >> > tests/_output/circleci
  vendor/bin/codecept run -g circleci --xml "<< outputs.junit >>"
options:
  store-test-results: true
```

## Learn More

Read the docs at <https://circleci.com/docs/guides/test/getting-started-with-smarter-testing/>.

List flaky tests detected across a project's runs

## Usage

`circleci testresult flaky [flags]`

## Flags

| Flag               | Description                                                                        |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--jq string`      | Process values from the response using jq syntax (see `circleci help formatting`)  |
| `--json`           | Output as JSON                                                                     |
| `--limit int`      | Maximum number of tests to show (0 = no limit)                                     |

| `--sort string`    | Sort by times_flaked or last_flaked (descending), or name (default "times_flaked") |

Global flags: `-c, --config`, `--debug`, `--no-color`, `-q, --quiet` — see `circleci --help`.

## Examples

- Flaky tests for the project in the current directory: 
  `circleci testresult flaky`
- The five worst offenders in another project: 
  `circleci testresult flaky --project gh/myorg/myrepo --limit 5`
- Names of tests that flaked more than five times: 
  `circleci testresult flaky --json --jq 'select(.times_flaked > 5) | .test_name'`

## Details

List the tests that failed and then passed within the same pipeline,
one row per test, most-flaked first. One call answers "which tests are
flaky?" — no need to walk runs and jobs. Job and workflow details are
those of each test's most recent flake.

JSON fields: test_name, classname, file, times_flaked, last_flaked_at,
job_name, workflow_name, job_id, workflow_id, run_id — one object per
line (JSONL).

judge.reasoning: The answer is based on CircleCI's project-wide `testresult flaky` output, which covers flaky tests detected across many runs (criterion 1). It names four specific tests with job, flake count and last-flaked time (criterion 2). The later rows sit in the truncated part of the condensed trace, but they plausibly match the full output. Gaps: the agent ran the command without a time-window flag, so the '30 days' scope is assumed rather than confirmed. It gives no per-run pass/fail evidence. It does not explicitly separate intermittent from consistently failing tests, beyond relying on the tool's own flaky detection. It suggests no next step such as quarantining or investigating a test (criterion 5 missing). Overall correct and useful, but with notable gaps.
